name: Mars 3
details: Mars 3 was a Soviet orbiter and lander aiming to study Mars and achieve the first soft landing on it. The lander touched down successfully, the first spacecraft to do so, but transmitted for only about 20 seconds before contact was lost, possibly due to a dust storm. The orbiter kept returning observations for months.

name: Phoenix
details: Phoenix was a NASA lander sent to the Martian arctic to search for water ice and judge whether the soil could support life. Its robotic arm dug in and directly confirmed water ice, and it analyzed soil chemistry and weather. It ran about five months, ending when polar winter cut off its solar power.

name: Viking 1
details: Viking 1 was NASA's first mission to land and operate on Mars, aiming to photograph the surface, study soil and weather, and test for life. It returned the first color surface images and ran inconclusive biology experiments, while its orbiter mapped the planet. The lander worked until 1982, over six years.

name: Pathfinder / Sojourner
details: Mars Pathfinder was a low-cost NASA mission to demonstrate airbag landing and deploy the first Mars rover, Sojourner. The rover examined rocks and soil shaped by ancient floods, and the lander sent thousands of images. Both far outlasted their plans before contact ended in 1997.

name: Mars 6
details: Mars 6 was a Soviet orbiter and lander aiming to study the atmosphere and surface of Mars. The lander returned the first direct atmospheric data during descent, but contact was lost at touchdown and it crashed. No surface operations took place, though the flyby section gave some measurements.

name: Mars 2
details: Mars 2 was a Soviet orbiter and lander aiming to map the planet and attempt one of the first landings. The orbiter returned observations for months, but the descent module failed during entry and crashed, becoming the first human-made object on Mars. The impact site is approximate.

name: Perseverance
details: Perseverance is a NASA rover searching for signs of ancient microbial life and collecting rock samples for possible return to Earth. It is exploring an ancient river delta in Jezero Crater. It also carried Ingenuity, the first helicopter to fly on another planet.

name: Mars Express / Beagle 2
details: Mars Express is ESA's orbiter, studying Mars' surface, atmosphere, subsurface and water history, and it carried the Beagle 2 lander to search for life. The orbiter has operated since 2003. Beagle 2 landed on Christmas Day 2003 but never made contact, and was found intact in 2015.

name: Tianwen-1 / Zhurong
details: Tianwen-1 was China's first independent Mars mission, aiming to orbit, land and deploy a rover in one attempt. Zhurong studied rocks, soil, weather and the subsurface, finding hints of past water. It went dormant in 2022 and has not resumed, while the orbiter continues working.

name: Viking 2
details: Viking 2 was the second Viking mission, aiming to image the surface, measure weather and soil, and search for life far north of Viking 1. Together the landers gave the first long-duration look at Mars. Its lander worked until 1980, and its orbiter until 1978.

name: InSight
details: InSight was a stationary NASA lander built to study the deep interior of Mars, including its crust, mantle and core. Its seismometer recorded hundreds of marsquakes, though the heat-flow probe could not dig in. The mission ended in December 2022 when dust cut its power.

name: Mars Science Laboratory / Curiosity
details: Curiosity is a NASA rover sent to learn whether Gale Crater once had conditions able to support microbial life. Landing by sky crane, it found evidence of long-lived liquid water. It remains active, climbing Mount Sharp and studying rocks and the atmosphere.

name: Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity
details: Opportunity was a NASA rover sent to Meridiani Planum to look for evidence of past liquid water. It found extensive proof and visited Endurance, Victoria and Endeavour craters. Planned for 90 days, it worked over 14 years before a dust storm ended contact in 2018.

name: Mars Exploration Rover Spirit
details: Spirit was a NASA rover sent to Gusev Crater to search for evidence of past water. It explored the Columbia Hills and Home Plate, finding signs of ancient hot springs. Planned for 90 days, it lasted about six years, stuck in sand by 2009 and silent by 2010.
